content.title: About
content.content: A cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a large beef patty, melted cheese, fresh vegetables, sauce, and a bun. This version uses one large patty (1682).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger was served in the 1920s in the United States.
The combination of beef and cheese makes the dish more filling and flavorful.
Cheeseburgers are often served with french fries and a soft drink.
Local variations exist: in Japan a teriyaki sauce is added, in India spices and meat‑free patties are common.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The patty provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and cheese contain B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: A cheeseburger provides quick satiety and a rapid energy boost, convenient for busy schedules.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cheeseburgers are rich in fats and carbohydrates, so they should be eaten in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: Cheese and sauces can increase saturated fat and sodium intake, which may affect cardiovascular health if consumed frequently.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Cheese contains dairy proteins that can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: Choose patties from reputable sources to reduce the risk of food‑borne illnesses.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburgers are typically eaten by hand, often split in half. They are commonly paired with fries, additional sauces, pickles, or a side salad. For a healthier twist, use a whole‑grain or gluten‑free bun.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped tightly in plastic. Reheat in an oven or microwave to retain bun crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Lime is a small green citrus fruit native to Southeast Asia. It has a bright, acidic flavor and aroma that are widely used in cooking, beverages, and cosmetics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lime belongs to the same genus as lemon, orange, and grapefruit.
There are several varieties, including Persian (Tahiti) and Mexican (Key) limes.
Lime became popular in Europe only in the 20th century after sea routes to the Caribbean were opened.
Lime juice is used in traditional medicine to ease colds and improve digestion.
Lime zest is rich in essential oils used in aromatherapy.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Lime provides high levels of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in lime help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Acids and enzymes in lime juice aid the digestion of proteins.

items.title: May reduce kidney stone risk
items.content: Citric acid present in lime can help prevent the formation of oxalate stones.

items.title: Improves skin health
items.content: Vitamin C and antioxidants promote wound healing and reduce hyperpigmentation.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to citrus fruits, including lime.

items.title: Tooth enamel erosion
items.content: The acidity of lime can contribute to enamel wear with frequent consumption.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Lime juice may increase the effect of certain medications, such as statins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lime is used as juice, zest, or wedges. Add it to drinks, sauces, marinades, salads, and desserts. Dried zest can be used as a fragrant seasoning.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store lime in the refrigerator in a plastic bag or the fruit drawer. At room temperature it stays fresh for 1‑2 days; refrigerated it lasts up to a week.

pasta-with-tomato-based-sauce-poultry-an.title: Pasta with tomato-based sauce, poultry, and added vegetables, ready-to-heat

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce, chicken and added vegetables is a ready‑to‑heat meal designed for quick preparation. It contains pasta, a tomato sauce, pieces of poultry meat and a mix of vegetables (carrot, broccoli, bell pepper). The dish provides a balanced amount of protein, carbohydrates and fiber, and can be stored in the fridge or freezer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tomato sauce supplies lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Chicken is usually pre‑seared, helping it stay juicy after reheating.
Vegetables are typically steamed to retain most of their vitamins.
The meal cooks in 2‑3 minutes in a microwave or on the stovetop.
It is popular in sports nutrition for its high protein content.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Chicken provides a complete source of animal protein essential for muscle repair.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: The sauce is rich in lycopene, which supports heart health and has anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: The vegetable mix adds dietary fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pasta supplies slowly released energy for sustained activity.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The dish contains vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, supporting immunity and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauces can be salty; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to chicken should avoid this product.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Ready‑made meals may contain preservatives; those sensitive should review the ingredient list.

items.title: Proper heating
items.content: Insufficient reheating may leave bacteria alive; heat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the portion in the microwave for 2‑3 minutes or on the stovetop, stirring halfway. Optionally garnish with fresh herbs, grated cheese or a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at +4 °C for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze at -18 °C, where it remains good for 2‑3 months. Thaw in the fridge before reheating.

content.title: About
content.content: A sweet roll with fruit and frosting is a soft baked treat covered with a thin layer of sugar glaze and filled with pieces of fresh fruit such as strawberry, kiwi or mango. The dough is usually made from a yeasted batter, giving it a light and airy texture. The glaze adds a gentle sweetness and shine, while the fruit filling provides aroma and a hint of tartness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of sweet fruit rolls originated in Japan, where they are known as “moti” with fruit filling.
Glaze is often made from powdered sugar, water, and a splash of lemon juice for a bright flavor.
Fruit fillings can be fresh or canned, allowing the product to stay fresh longer.
Sweet rolls are commonly served at celebrations and as a tea-time dessert.
In some countries the rolls are decorated with edible flowers for visual appeal.

items.title: Vitamins from fruit
items.content: The fruit filling is rich in vitamins C and A, which support immune function and vision.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The roll provides a quick source of energy thanks to carbohydrates from the dough and sugar.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fruit adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Berries and other fruits contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sweet taste and bright colors can lift mood and reduce stress.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Glaze and fruit syrups can be high in sugar, which is a concern for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The dough may contain gluten, and some fruits (e.g., strawberries) are common allergens.

items.title: Acidity of fruit
items.content: Citrus or tart fruits may irritate a sensitive stomach in some individuals.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Fresh fruit spoils quickly, so rolls should be refrigerated and consumed within a few days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sweet fruit roll chilled or at room temperature. It is easy to eat with hands, breaking off bite‑size pieces. For extra crunch, sprinkle with powdered sugar or chopped nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep rolls in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze them wrapped in plastic film and thaw at room temperature before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Steak sauce is a thick, flavorful condiment designed for serving with grilled or pan‑seared meats, especially steaks. It typically contains a tomato base, vinegar, spices, sugar, and sometimes soy sauce, giving it a sweet‑tart taste with a hint of heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial steak sauce appeared in the United States in the early 20th century.
Traditional recipes often include anchovies, which add an umami depth.
In Japan, a popular “teriyaki” style mixes the sauce with honey and ginger.
Gluten‑free versions replace wheat flour with corn starch.
Steak sauce is frequently used as a marinade, allowing meat to absorb flavor for several hours.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and spices provide lycopene and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar and certain spices stimulate gastric juice production, aiding protein digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike creamy sauces, steak sauce usually contains little fat, making it a lighter option.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some varieties are sweetened, so people monitoring blood sugar should choose reduced‑sugar versions.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: High salt content can be an issue for those with hypertension; check the label.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Ingredients may include soy, mustard, or dairy—verify the list if you have allergies.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the sauce with hot steaks, burgers, grilled meat, or even roasted vegetables. It can be used as a marinade by coating meat 2‑4 hours before cooking, or as a glaze applied a few minutes before the end of grilling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce refrigerated after opening in a tightly sealed jar. Once opened, it typically remains good for 3‑6 months. Discard if you notice off‑smell, color changes, or mold.

tea-iced-brewed-black-pre-sweetened-with.title: Tea, iced, brewed, black, pre‑sweetened with low calorie sweetener

content.title: About
content.content: A ready‑to‑drink iced black tea brewed from Camellia sinensis leaves and pre‑sweetened with a low‑calorie sweetener (code 5269). The beverage contains no sugar but retains the characteristic aroma and strength of black tea.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea is rich in polyphenols that may support cardiovascular health.
Cold‑brewed tea preserves most of the antioxidants found in hot tea.
Low‑calorie sweeteners reduce the energy content while keeping the sweet taste.
The product is convenient for on‑the‑go consumption – no additional brewing required.
Black tea has a long cultural history, from British afternoon tea to Asian iced tea drinks.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Polyphenols in black tea help neutralize free radicals, supporting cellular health.

items.title: Improved focus
items.content: Caffeine in black tea enhances attention and cognitive performance without a sudden energy spike.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The low‑calorie sweetener allows a sweet taste without adding significant calories.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Iced tea contributes to daily fluid intake, especially in warm weather.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Tannins in black tea may aid digestion and reduce the feeling of heaviness after meals.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience nervousness, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat with excessive caffeine.

items.title: Allergy to sweetener
items.content: Rare allergic reactions to the low‑calorie sweetener are possible.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain central nervous system stimulants.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Tea may increase stomach acidity, which can be problematic for gastritis or ulcer patients.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the iced tea straight from the package or pour it over ice in a glass. Optionally add a slice of lemon, fresh mint, or berries to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 7–10 days for best quality.
